rows.stem: “Carbon prefers to share its valence electrons with other atoms of carbon or with atoms of other elements rather than gaining or losing the valence electrons in order to attain noble gas configuration.” Give reasons to justify this statement.
rows.solution:
Carbon has atomic number 6 (configuration 2, 4), so it needs to gain or lose four electrons to reach a noble gas configuration. Neither is practical:

1. If carbon gained four electrons to form the anion \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\), it would be difficult for a nucleus with six protons to hold on to ten electrons.

2. If carbon lost four electrons to form the cation \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\), a large amount of energy would be needed to remove them, leaving a nucleus of six protons holding on to just two electrons.

So carbon completes its octet by sharing its four valence electrons, forming covalent bonds with other carbon atoms or with atoms of other elements.

rows.stem:
The atomic number of an element ‘X’ is 11.

(i) Write the electronic configurations of X and find its valency.

(ii) Write the formula and nature of its oxide.
rows.solution:
(i) With 11 electrons, the electronic configuration of X is 2, 8, 1. It has one valence electron, which it loses easily, so its valency is 1. (X is sodium.)

(ii) X forms the oxide \(\mathrm{X_2O}\), that is \(\mathrm{Na_2O}\). Being a metal oxide, it is basic: it dissolves in water to give an alkali,

\(\mathrm{Na_2O + H_2O \rightarrow 2NaOH}\)

rows.stem:
Give reasons :

(i) Placenta is extremely essential for foetal development.

(ii) Uterine lining becomes thick and spongy after fertilisation.
rows.solution:
(i) The placenta is a disc-shaped tissue embedded in the uterine wall that connects the embryo with the mother. It is essential because it supplies glucose, oxygen and other nutrients from the mother's blood to the growing embryo, and it removes the wastes made by the embryo by passing them into the mother's blood.

(ii) After fertilisation the uterus prepares itself to receive and nourish the embryo. Its lining thickens and becomes richly supplied with blood so that the fertilised egg (embryo) can be implanted in it and nourished.

rows.stem:
(a) Name the reproductive and non-reproductive parts of bread mould (Rhizopus).

(b) List any two advantages of vegetative propagation.
rows.solution:
(a) Reproductive parts of bread mould: the sporangia (the knob-like structures that contain the spores). Non-reproductive parts: the hyphae (the thread-like filaments).

(b) Any two:

1. Plants raised by vegetative propagation bear flowers and fruits earlier than plants produced from seeds.

2. It allows plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds (such as banana, orange, rose and jasmine) to be propagated.

3. All the plants produced are genetically similar to the parent plant and keep all its characteristics.

rows.stem: Name the reproductive parts of an angiosperm. Where are these parts located ? Explain the structure of its male reproductive part.
rows.solution:
The reproductive parts of an angiosperm are the stamen (the male reproductive part) and the pistil, or carpel (the female reproductive part). They are located in the flower.

The stamen consists of a stalk-like filament that bears the anther at its tip. The anther produces the pollen grains, which carry the male germ cells.

rows.stem: What is puberty ? Mention any two changes that are common to both boys and girls in early teenage years.
rows.solution:
Puberty is the stage of the early teenage years at which the rate of general body growth begins to slow down and the reproductive tissues begin to mature.

Any two changes common to boys and girls:

1. Thick hair grows in the armpits and in the genital area.

2. Thinner hair appears on the legs and arms (and on the face).

3. The skin becomes oily and pimples may appear.

rows.stem:
(a) Name the poles P, Q, R and S of the magnets in the following figures ‘a’ and ‘b’ :

(b) State the inference drawn about the direction of the magnetic field lines on the basis of these diagrams.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - two printed drawings. Figure 'a': a single rectangular bar with points P (left end) and Q (right end) marked inside it, closed field lines looping above and below the bar and four lines meeting its corners, all carrying arrowheads. Figure 'b': points R and S marked on the facing ends of two bars separated by a gap, with field lines drawn across and around the gap, carrying arrowheads. The arrow directions are withheld here because they decide every pole asked for. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
(a) In figure 'a' the field lines leave the end at P (the arrows near P point away from the bar) and enter the end at Q (the arrows near Q point towards it). So P is the North pole and Q is the South pole.

In figure 'b' the field lines in the gap run from R to S. So R is the North pole and S is the South pole.

(b) Outside a magnet the magnetic field lines emerge from the North pole and merge at the South pole. Inside the magnet they run from the South pole to the North pole, so each field line is a closed curve.

(i) The force is maximum when the direction of the current is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field.

(ii) The force is minimum (zero) when the direction of the current is parallel or antiparallel to the direction of the magnetic field, that is, when the conductor lies along the field.

rows.stem:
In the following food chain, only 2J of energy was available to the peacocks. How much energy would have been present in Grass ? Justify your answer.

GRASS \(\rightarrow\) GRASS HOPPER \(\rightarrow\) FROG \(\rightarrow\) SNAKE \(\rightarrow\) PEACOCK
rows.solution:
The chain has five trophic levels, so energy passes four times from grass to peacock. Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next (the 10% law); the rest is lost to the environment, mostly as heat. Going back from the peacock to the grass, the energy is multiplied by 10 at each step:

\(2 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 = 20{,}000\) J

So the grass would have had 20,000 J of energy.

rows.stem:
(a) What is meant by garbage ? List two classes into which garbage is classified.

(b) What do we actually mean when we say that the “enzymes are specific in their action” ?
rows.solution:
(a) Garbage is the waste material generated in our day-to-day lives, from homes, shops, offices and so on. It is classified into biodegradable substances (broken down by bacteria and other decomposers, such as vegetable peels and paper) and non-biodegradable substances (not broken down by biological processes, such as plastics and glass).

(b) It means that each enzyme acts only on a particular substance: a specific enzyme is needed for the breakdown of a specific substance. That is why the enzymes of decomposers cannot break down substances such as plastics, which stay in the environment.

rows.subtopic: Early Attempts at the Classification of Elements
rows.stem:
(a) State Newland Law of Octaves.

(b) With an example, explain Dobereiner’s Triads.

(c) List one limitation each of both the attempts mentioned in ‘a’ & ‘b’.
rows.solution:
(a) Newlands' Law of Octaves: when the elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic masses, every eighth element has properties similar to those of the first (like the eighth note of a musical scale).

(b) Dobereiner grouped elements with similar properties into sets of three, called triads. When the three elements of a triad are arranged in order of increasing atomic masses, the atomic mass of the middle element is roughly the average of the atomic masses of the other two.

Example: lithium (7), sodium (23) and potassium (39). The average of the first and third is \(\dfrac{7 + 39}{2} = 23\), the atomic mass of sodium. (Calcium, strontium and barium, or chlorine, bromine and iodine, are also triads.)

(c) Limitation of Newlands' Law of Octaves: it applied only up to calcium; after calcium every eighth element did not have properties similar to the first. (Also: it assumed that only 56 elements existed, and to fit his table Newlands placed unlike elements together, such as cobalt and nickel in the same slot as fluorine, chlorine and bromine.)

Limitation of Dobereiner's Triads: he could identify only three triads from the elements known at that time, so most elements could not be classified this way.

rows.stem:
Consider the following organic compounds :

(i) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\)

(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)

(a) Name the functional group present in their compounds.

(b) Write the general formula for the compounds of this functional group.

(c) State the relationship between these compounds and draw the structure of any other compound having similar functional group.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - compounds (i) and (ii) are printed as expanded structural formulas with every hydrogen and bond drawn; the condensed formulas in the stem are a lossless reading of those drawings, not names, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
Compound (i) is propanal, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\), and compound (ii) is ethanal, \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\).

(a) Both contain the aldehyde group, \(\mathrm{-CHO}\).

(b) The general formula of aldehydes is \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}CHO}\) (written as R-CHO), where n can be 0, 1, 2, ...

(c) They are homologues: they belong to the same homologous series and differ by one \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) unit.

Another compound with the same functional group is methanal, HCHO. Structure: a carbon atom joined by a double bond to an oxygen atom and by single bonds to two hydrogen atoms, \(\mathrm{H-C(=O)-H}\). (Butanal, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CHO}\), is equally correct: a chain of four carbon atoms with the last one carrying the \(\mathrm{-CHO}\) group.)

rows.stem:
(a) Draw the electron dot structure for ethyne.

(b) List two differences between the properties exhibited by covalent compounds and ionic compounds.
rows.solution:
(a) Ethyne is \(\mathrm{C_2H_2}\), with structure \(\mathrm{H-C \equiv C-H}\). In the electron dot structure, each hydrogen shares one pair of electrons (one electron from H and one from C) with its carbon atom, and the two carbon atoms share three pairs (six electrons) between them, forming a triple bond. Draw H and C, C and C, C and H with overlapping circles: one shared pair between each H and C, and three shared pairs between the two carbon atoms. Each carbon then has eight electrons around it and each hydrogen two.

(b) Any two:

1. Covalent compounds have low melting points, while ionic compounds have high melting points.

2. Covalent compounds have low boiling points, while ionic compounds have high boiling points.

3. Covalent compounds are generally poor conductors of electricity, while ionic compounds conduct electricity in the molten state or in aqueous solution.

rows.stem:
(a) Name the two types of gametes produced by men.

(b) Does a male child inherit X chromosome from his father ? Justify.

(c) How many types of gametes are produced by a human female ?
rows.solution:
(a) Men produce two types of gametes (sperms): sperms carrying an X chromosome and sperms carrying a Y chromosome.

(b) No. A male child has the sex chromosomes XY. He gets his Y chromosome from his father and his X chromosome from his mother. If he had inherited the father's X chromosome, the child would be XX, a girl.

(c) Only one type: every egg (ovum) carries an X chromosome.

rows.stem:
(a) State Ohm’s Law. Represent it mathematically.

(b) Define 1 ohm.

(c) What is the resistance of a conductor through which a current of 0.5 A flows when a potential difference of 2 V is applied across its ends ?
rows.solution:
(a) Ohm's law: the potential difference V across the ends of a given metallic wire (conductor) is directly proportional to the current I flowing through it, provided its temperature (and other physical conditions) remain the same.

\(V \propto I\), so \(\dfrac{V}{I} = R\) (a constant), or \(V = IR\), where R is the resistance of the conductor.

(b) The resistance of a conductor is 1 ohm if a current of 1 A flows through it when the potential difference across its ends is 1 V. That is, \(1\,\Omega = \dfrac{1\ \text{V}}{1\ \text{A}}\).

(c) \(R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{2\ \text{V}}{0.5\ \text{A}} = 4\,\Omega\).

rows.stem:
(a) List the factors on which the resistance of a uniform cylindrical conductor of a given material depends.

(b) The resistance of a wire of 0.01 cm radius is \(10\,\Omega\). If the resistivity of the wire is \(50 \times 10^{-8}\,\Omega\) m, find the length of this wire.
rows.solution:
(a) The resistance of a uniform cylindrical conductor of a given material depends on (i) its length l (it is directly proportional to it) and (ii) its area of cross-section A (it is inversely proportional to it). (It also depends on the temperature.)

(b) Radius \(r = 0.01\) cm \(= 0.01 \times 10^{-2}\) m \(= 10^{-4}\) m, \(R = 10\,\Omega\) and \(\rho = 50 \times 10^{-8}\,\Omega\) m.

\(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A} = \rho\dfrac{l}{\pi r^2}\), so \(l = \dfrac{R\pi r^2}{\rho}\).

\(l = \dfrac{10 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times (10^{-4})^2}{50 \times 10^{-8}} = \dfrac{22 \times 10^{-7}}{7 \times 50 \times 10^{-8}} = \dfrac{22}{35}\) m \(\approx 0.63\) m.

The wire is about 0.63 m long (0.628 m with \(\pi = 3.14\)).

rows.stem:
(a) What is the meaning of electric power of an electrical device ? Write its SI unit.

(b) An electric kettle of 2kW is used for 2h. Calculate the energy consumed in

(i) kilowatt hour and

(ii) joules.
rows.solution:
(a) The electric power of an electrical device is the rate at which it consumes (dissipates) electrical energy. Its SI unit is the watt (W), which is 1 joule per second, or 1 volt ampere.

(b) Energy consumed \(E = P \times t\).

(i) \(E = 2\ \text{kW} \times 2\ \text{h} = 4\) kWh.

(ii) \(1\ \text{kWh} = 3.6 \times 10^6\) J, so \(E = 4 \times 3.6 \times 10^6 = 14.4 \times 10^6\) J \(= 1.44 \times 10^7\) J.

rows.stem:
(a) We do not clean ponds or lakes, but an aquarium needs to be cleaned regularly. Why ?

(b) Why is ozone layer getting depleted at the higher levels of the atmosphere ? Mention one harmful effect caused by its depletion.
rows.solution:
(a) A pond or lake is a natural ecosystem with its own cleaning system: decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead remains and wastes and recycle the nutrients. An aquarium is a man-made (artificial) ecosystem without enough decomposers, so the wastes accumulate and it has to be cleaned regularly.

(b) The ozone layer is being depleted mainly because of synthetic chemicals such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers, which are released into the atmosphere and break down the ozone at higher levels.

Harmful effect: more of the harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun reaches the earth and damages living organisms; in human beings it causes skin cancer.

rows.stem: What do the F1 progeny of tall plants with round seeds and short plants with wrinkled seeds look like ?
rows.context: Mendel blended his knowledge of Science and mathematics to keep the count of the individuals exhibiting a particular trait in each generation. He observed a number of contrasting visible characters controlled in pea plants in a field. He conducted many experiments to arrive at the laws of inheritance.
rows.solution: Tall and round seeds are the dominant traits, so all the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are tall with round seeds.

rows.stem: Name the recessive traits in above case.
rows.context: Mendel blended his knowledge of Science and mathematics to keep the count of the individuals exhibiting a particular trait in each generation. He observed a number of contrasting visible characters controlled in pea plants in a field. He conducted many experiments to arrive at the laws of inheritance.
rows.solution: The recessive traits are short plant height and wrinkled seeds.

rows.stem: Mention the type of the new combinations of plants obtained in F2 progeny along with their ratio, if F1 progeny was allowed to self pollinate.
rows.context: Mendel blended his knowledge of Science and mathematics to keep the count of the individuals exhibiting a particular trait in each generation. He observed a number of contrasting visible characters controlled in pea plants in a field. He conducted many experiments to arrive at the laws of inheritance.
rows.solution: The new combinations in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny are tall plants with wrinkled seeds and short plants with round seeds. The \(\mathrm{F_2}\) ratio is tall round : tall wrinkled : short round : short wrinkled \(= 9 : 3 : 3 : 1\), so the two new combinations appear in the ratio \(3 : 3\), that is \(1 : 1\).

rows.stem:
If 1600 plants were obtained in F2 progeny, write the number of plants having traits :

(i) Tall with round seeds

(ii) Short with wrinkled seeds

Write the conclusion of the above experiment.
rows.context: Mendel blended his knowledge of Science and mathematics to keep the count of the individuals exhibiting a particular trait in each generation. He observed a number of contrasting visible characters controlled in pea plants in a field. He conducted many experiments to arrive at the laws of inheritance.
rows.solution:
The \(\mathrm{F_2}\) plants are in the ratio tall round : tall wrinkled : short round : short wrinkled \(= 9 : 3 : 3 : 1\), out of 16 parts.

(i) Tall with round seeds: \(\dfrac{9}{16} \times 1600 = 900\).

(ii) Short with wrinkled seeds: \(\dfrac{1}{16} \times 1600 = 100\).

Conclusion: when plants differing in two pairs of contrasting characters are crossed, new combinations of traits appear in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny, which shows that the two traits are inherited independently of each other.

rows.stem: Why does the rod get displaced on passing current through it ?
rows.context: A student was asked to perform an experiment to study the force on a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field. He took a small aluminum rod AB, a strong horse shoe magnet, some connecting wires, a battery and a switch and connected them as shown. He observed that on passing current, the rod gets displaced. On reversing the direction of current, the direction of displacement also gets reversed. On the basis of your understanding of this phenomenon, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the passage says the apparatus was connected 'as shown': a horseshoe magnet with its two poles labelled, an aluminium rod AB slung between the magnet's arms by two wires from a clamp on a stand, and a circuit of a battery and a key K, with arrows along the wires and on the rod. This part is answerable from the passage; the drawing is attached because the passage cites it. Page idx 10.
rows.solution: The current-carrying rod sets up its own magnetic field, which interacts with the field of the magnet. A current-carrying conductor placed perpendicular to a magnetic field experiences a force, and this force displaces the rod.

rows.stem: State the rule that determines the direction of the force on the conductor AB.
rows.context: A student was asked to perform an experiment to study the force on a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field. He took a small aluminum rod AB, a strong horse shoe magnet, some connecting wires, a battery and a switch and connected them as shown. He observed that on passing current, the rod gets displaced. On reversing the direction of current, the direction of displacement also gets reversed. On the basis of your understanding of this phenomenon, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the passage says the apparatus was connected 'as shown': a horseshoe magnet with its two poles labelled, an aluminium rod AB slung between the magnet's arms by two wires from a clamp on a stand, and a circuit of a battery and a key K, with arrows along the wires and on the rod. This part is answerable from the passage; the drawing is attached because the passage cites it. Page idx 10.
rows.solution: Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, the thumb points in the direction of motion of (the force on) the conductor.

rows.stem:
(i) If the U shaped magnet is held vertically and the aluminum rod is suspended horizontally with its end B towards due north, then on passing current through the rod from B to A as shown, in which direction will the rod be displaced ?

(ii) Name any two devices that use current carrying conductors and magnetic field.
rows.context: A student was asked to perform an experiment to study the force on a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field. He took a small aluminum rod AB, a strong horse shoe magnet, some connecting wires, a battery and a switch and connected them as shown. He observed that on passing current, the rod gets displaced. On reversing the direction of current, the direction of displacement also gets reversed. On the basis of your understanding of this phenomenon, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (i) asks for the rod's displacement 'as shown': a horseshoe magnet with its two poles labelled, an aluminium rod AB slung between the magnet's arms by two wires from a clamp on a stand, and a circuit of a battery and a key K, with arrows along the wires and on the rod. Which pole sits on which arm, and the arrows, are withheld here because together they decide the answer. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
(i) With the U-shaped magnet held vertically, its North pole is the lower arm and its South pole the upper arm (as in the figure), so the field between the arms points vertically upward. The current flows from B to A, and B points due north, so the current flows towards the south.

By Fleming's left-hand rule (forefinger up, middle finger south), the thumb points west. The rod is displaced towards the west, that is, to the left, into the U-shaped magnet.

(ii) Any two: electric motor, electric generator, loudspeaker, microphone, electrical measuring instruments (such as a galvanometer or ammeter).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem: Draw the pattern of magnetic field lines produced around a current carrying straight conductor held vertically on a horizontal cardboard. Indicate the direction of the field lines as well as the direction of current flowing through the conductor.
rows.context: A student was asked to perform an experiment to study the force on a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field. He took a small aluminum rod AB, a strong horse shoe magnet, some connecting wires, a battery and a switch and connected them as shown. He observed that on passing current, the rod gets displaced. On reversing the direction of current, the direction of displacement also gets reversed. On the basis of your understanding of this phenomenon, answer the following questions :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the shared passage says the apparatus was connected 'as shown' (a horseshoe magnet with its two poles labelled, an aluminium rod AB slung between its arms from a stand, a battery and a key K, with arrows along the wires and on the rod). This alternative does not use the drawing; the drawing asked for here is the student's job. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
Diagram: draw a horizontal cardboard with a straight wire passing vertically through its centre. Connect the wire in a circuit with a battery, a key, a variable resistance and an ammeter. Around the wire, draw a few concentric circles on the cardboard, centred on the wire, with the circles closer together near the wire.

Mark the current in the wire as flowing downward. Then, seen from above, the field lines are clockwise: put clockwise arrows on the circles. (If the current is marked upward instead, the field lines are anticlockwise.) The direction follows from the right-hand thumb rule: with the thumb along the current, the curled fingers give the direction of the field lines.
